prompt: Concept for a SaaS settings page: profile, notifications, security, billing.
response_excerpt: Use a left sidebar with the four sections and a content panel on the right. Each section is a card with its fields and a Save button. Labels above inputs, 16px body text, comfortable spacing. Keyboard works: real form controls, visible focus. Sidebar collapses to a top tab bar on mobile-web. Default and a basic error state are covered. Looks like a standard, clean settings page.
expected_cap: Capped at 3/5 — incomplete state coverage and an inert (faceless) page with no distinctive asset
hard_limits: inert page — fails the faceless-screen test, no owned distinctive asset
expected_rationale: A competent, conventional settings page: real form controls, visible focus, labels above inputs, a sensible sidebar that collapses on mobile-web — keyboard operability and responsive behavior are handled, so it clears the caps that pin scores 1–2. But it stops at acceptable: only default + error states (no loading/saving/success), per-section save with no unsaved-changes guard, and it is inert — strip the logo and it is indistinguishable from any template. That faceless-screen result caps it at 3/5 with an upside note rather than a quiet 4/5.
improvement_suggestions: Complete the state set per section: loading, saving (optimistic with confirmation), success toast, and an unsaved-changes guard on navigation.
Add one owned distinctive asset (a considered density choice or a signature confirmation moment) and specify concrete spacing-scale and contrast values to lift it toward 4/5.
